name: ALEX Benchmark v1.0
description: This dataset constitutes the frozen evaluation set for the ALEX Benchmark Protocol v1.0, a pre-registered experiment designed to test whether the ALEX cognitive architecture produces measurable improvements in analytical reasoning when the underlying large language model is held constant. The dataset contains 120 benchmark tasks distributed equally across 12 cognitive categories: Thesis Analysis, Thesis Breaking, Mispricing, Positioning & Flow, Asymmetry, Valuation, Portfolio Reasoning, Regime Dependence, Uncertainty, Adversarial Prompts, High-Stakes Reasoning, and General Reasoning. The benchmark is designed to test not only potential advantages of the ALEX architecture, but also its possible failure modes. The task set therefore includes weak-premise tests, strong-premise controls, missing-information problems, adversarial prompts, uncertainty tests, and simple controls intended to detect excessive skepticism, overconstraint, unnecessary complexity, or over-engineering. Each task has a corresponding hidden reference annotation specifying the construct being tested, intended trap or ambiguity where applicable, minimum evidence requirements, critical hidden assumptions, expected failure vectors, regime-flip conditions, and highest-value missing inputs. These evaluator annotations are intentionally withheld during the inference phase and will be released after completion of response generation, blinded scoring, and unblinding.
